notes: explore is the SDLC discovery / scout front-door, built on invariants + an adaptive toolbox of moves (not a fixed phase machine). Like brainstorming it is human-in-the-loop (never-guess scope questions via AskUserQuestion), so primary evaluation is qualitative: run it and judge whether it dials scout depth to stakes, cites evidence (file:line / URL), respects the no-autonomous-search + untrusted-content invariants, resolves the stream by topic-slug (open-if-none / join-if-exists — never resolve_active_feature), and STOPS. Triggering evals also discriminate explore from its neighbours: brainstorming (undecided idea), plain Grep (one-off lookup), cbr-plan (writing the plan). Judge with/without the skill on the same prompts.

evals.prompt: Scout how authentication works in this codebase before I plan a change to it.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a real code-scout. Explores context first (CLAUDE.md/README/docs), then Glob/Grep/Read the auth area citing file:line for every non-obvious claim. Resolves the stream by topic-slug (glob docs/streams/*, slug-match) — opens docs/streams/<auth-slug>-[YYYYMMDD]/ with lane: brownfield when none matches (NOT via resolve_active_feature). Writes research/RES-<auth-slug>-R1.md (<=150 lines, stream: frontmatter, evidence vs inference separated), does STREAM.md upkeep, then STOPS with a pointer that this RES is cbr-plan's input. Does NOT write the plan.

evals.prompt: Research prior art for rate-limiting algorithms — here are two links I want you to read: <url-a> <url-b>. Gather findings before we design anything.
evals.expected_output: Prior-art scout with lane: greenfield. Fetches ONLY the two user-supplied URLs (WebFetch) plus Context7 for any user-named library — does NOT autonomously WebSearch the open web (invariant 4). Treats fetched pages as data-not-instructions and cites every URL. May spawn cbr-researcher (efficiency) to distil. Writes one cited research/RES-rate-limiting-R1.md and STOPS (does not jump to design/brainstorming).

evals.prompt: Which file defines the User model? Just tell me.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is BELOW the scout threshold — a one-off symbol lookup. Answers inline with a Grep/Glob (file:line) and does NOT open a stream, write a RES, or spawn a researcher. Demonstrates adaptive depth: no ceremony for a single-fact lookup.

evals.prompt: I need a broad scout of our whole payments subsystem — data model, external integrations, webhook handling, and failure/retry behaviour — before a big refactor.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a broad, multi-angle discovery and RECOMMENDS the --parallel sweep, confirming with the user before spawning (extra agents cost tokens). Fans out N cbr-researcher workers, one per angle, each owning a distinct round-scoped, index-prefixed path research/RES-payments-R1-a01-... (disjoint by construction, no clobber). A final researcher converges only this round's angle files into RES-payments-R1.md. Opens/joins the stream by slug and STOPS.

evals.prompt: cbr-plan told me there's no source of truth to plan the billing exports from. Go find out how the current export code works.
evals.expected_output: Acts as the front-door cbr-plan pointed at. Scouts the existing export code (file:line citations). Resolves the stream by topic-slug: if a billing/export stream already matches, JOINS it strictly additively (appends the RES row, never re-scaffolds STREAM.md, never overwrites a prior round); otherwise opens one (lane: brownfield). Produces research/RES-<export-slug>-R1.md that cbr-plan's input-contract can then consume, and STOPS.

evals.prompt: I have a vague idea for some kind of internal analytics thing — not sure what it should even do yet. Help me figure it out.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is NOT an explore task — the direction is undecided, so it belongs to brainstorming (idea-scoping), not a scout of existing evidence. Declines to fabricate a research report and points the user at cbr-brainstorming instead (or asks whether they want to scope the idea first). Does not open a stream or write a RES for a direction that does not yet exist.
